question: How can an unauthenticated threat actor exploit CVE-2026-41940 in cPanel & WHM versions prior to 118.0.9, 116.0.15, 112.0.34, and 108.0.26 to gain administrative access, and what technical details differentiate this zero-day from N-day CVEs in the same product line?
answer:
CVE-2026-41940 is a critical authentication bypass in cPanel & WHM that results from a race condition in the “/login/” endpoint combined with a missing input sanitization step in the session creation logic. The flaw manifests when a malformed HTTP POST request containing a manipulated Referer header triggers a path traversal in the session cookie generation routine. Specifically, the vulnerable code in /usr/local/cpanel/base/frontend/paper_lantern/login/index.html.php (affected in builds prior to 118.0.9) fails to canonicalize the URI before constructing the session ID, allowing a threat actor to craft a Referer header like https://victim.com/..%2f..%2f..%2f..%2fvar%2fcpanel%2fbandwidth to leak the existing administrator’s session token via a timing side-channel. This behavior is not present in N-day CVEs such as CVE-2023-29489 (XSS in cpsrvd) or CVE-2024-36540 (hard-coded credential), which require previous authentication or predictable credentials—the zero-day instead pivots from no session to full admin in a single request.

Exploitation vector:
1. Send a crafted HTTP POST to https://<cp_host>:2083/login/ with Referer: https://victim.com/..%2f..%2f..%2f..%2fvar%2fcpanel%2fsessions%2fadmin_sess
2. Monitor the Set-Cookie header for the administrator’s existing PHPSESSID.
3. Replay that session cookie to /cpanel/index.html, yielding an authenticated cPanel dashboard without credentials.

Tooling: A Metasploit module (auxiliary/admin/http/cpanel_auth_bypass_cve_2026_41940) automates the header manipulation, while Burp Suite’s Turbo Intruder can be tuned with a 20 ms timing delay to maximize token leak probability. Proof-of-concept code on GitHub uses curl with –referer and –cookie-jar to script the theft.

Mitigation:
• Upgrade to the patched releases 118.0.9, 116.0.15, 112.0.34, or 108.0.26.
• Apply cPanel’s official hotpatch H-2026-04-30 which replaces the vulnerable index.html.php with a version that canonicalizes URIs via realpath() before session token generation.
• Enable “Require SSL for all logins” in WHM → Tweak Settings and enforce HSTS at the load balancer to mitigate side-channel leakage.

Real-world impact: In early May 2026, the threat actor “UNC5733” weaponized CVE-2026-41940 across 3,800 exposed cPanel hosts, achieving domain admin on shared-hosting providers and subsequently pivoting via SSH key extraction. The campaign replicated across shodan-identified instances within 72 hours, underscoring the need for zero-touch patching in hosting environments.
